stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes (H R 5334)
votes.bill_title: Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 93)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes it, except for forces needed to defend against an imminent attack if the President follows the War Powers Resolution's time limits. A Yea agrees. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 89)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea agrees to that direction. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon (H CON RES 108)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon within seven days of the resolution's adoption. A Yea agrees to the concurrent resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Ukraine Support Act (H R 2913)
votes.plain_language: This bill addresses the war between Russia and Ukraine by (1) providing assistance to Ukraine and certain European countries, and (2) establishing penalties for Russia and certain foreign persons (individuals and entities). A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from Lebanon (H CON RES 84)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from Lebanon.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from Lebanon within seven days of the resolution's adoption. A Yea agrees to the concurrent resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 86)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran unless explicitly authorized by a declaration of war or a congressional authorization for use of military force against Iran. A Yea agrees to the concurrent resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran (H CON RES 75)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran or any part of its government or military no later than March 30, 2026, unless a declaration of war or authorization to use military force for such purpose has been enacted. A Yea agrees to the concurrent resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — To require the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status (H R 1689)
votes.bill_title: To require the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status.
votes.plain_language: This bill directs the Department of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status for 18 months beginning August 3, 2025. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 40)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran unless explicitly authorized by a declaration of war or a congressional authorization for use of military force against Iran. A Yea agrees to the concurrent resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from unauthorized hostilities in the Islamic Republic of Iran (H CON RES 38)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from unauthorized hostilities in the Islamic Republic of Iran.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution directs the President to terminate the use of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran or any part of the Iranian government or military unless a declaration of war or authorization to use military force for such purpose has been enacted. A Yea agrees to the concurrent resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Agree — Reaffirming Iran remains the largest state sponsor of terrorism (H RES 1099)
votes.bill_title: Reaffirming Iran remains the largest state sponsor of terrorism.
votes.plain_language: This resolution states that the House of Representatives declares it is the policy of the United States that Iran continues to be the largest state sponsor of terrorism. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports agreeing to it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — PROTECT Taiwan Act (H R 1531)
votes.plain_language: This bill requires certain federal entities to seek to exclude China from six international financial organizations if the President informs Congress that China's actions threaten Taiwan and pose a danger to U.S. interests. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — To direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from Venezuela that have not been authorized by Congress (H CON RES 68)
votes.bill_title: To direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from Venezuela that have not been authorized by Congress.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from Venezuela unless a declaration of war or authorization to use military force for such purpose has been enacted. A Yea agrees to the concurrent resolution; a Nay opposes it.

posts.text: This is why I became a @JonPardi fan this weekend. Watch: https://t.co/94VCITBAHV

Thank you to the Peoria Police and the FBI for arresting the suspect responsible for planting a bomb at BioUrja.

We must find out why this person would want to threaten our neighbors in such a manner, and bring swift justice for the potential harm this action could’ve done. https://t.co/Ln2skH5W6U
This is what supporting your neighbors looks like. https://t.co/qsK9UZdXzZ
Threat for Peoria explosion is over. https://t.co/R9mdFOkxR9

🚨 The City of Peoria has set up a special phone number to call for info. 309-673-4527. Share this with your neighbors, and do not hesitate to call with any questions or concerns about the ongoing evacuation.

More updates from Peoria as I get info. https://t.co/U61oaAHFDi

Continue to pray for the safety and well-being of law enforcement on scene at BioUrja in Peoria. Essential: We must make sure that everyone stays one mile away from the plant. 

It may take much of the day or even the weekend before officials can give an ‘all clear.’ An update is https://t.co/xYtf2ph7LQ
Update as of now in Peoria. https://t.co/UIflPsq9i0

https://t.co/RYVezwTCyY

https://t.co/G1R1KkKZws

My team and I are monitoring the evacuation of parts of Downtown Peoria this Friday evening. Please heed all instructions!

Thank you to the Peoria Police Department, the Illinois State Police, and all first responders who immediately took action to keep our neighbors safe. 

I have reached out to Mayor Ali and offered any assistance. Stay safe! 

Links to WMBD and WEEK News updates in comments.
https://t.co/aHE5efU9YY…

Did you know farmers in the Midwest—especially here in Illinois—have paid much more than they've gotten out of the Federal Crop Insurance Program? And they’ve overpaid for DECADES!
 
As farmers struggle with the high cost of diesel, inputs, and more, we need to level the playing field before they’re forced to leave the federal program altogether. I sat down with Noah from @agripulse to talk about my legislation to fix this. 🔗⬇️

A few weeks ago, my team crossed $5 million rightfully returned to our neighbors…just in the past two years!

Getting IRS situations rectified, VA benefits delivered, and social security cases closed means the world to so many people and I am so proud of our team.

Looking https://t.co/qp7vz9XSAC

Happy Veterans Day!

Today, and every day, I'm grateful for the service and sacrifice of our veterans and military families. https://t.co/Q7OVgAMBOZ

Grateful to join ASTRO America Advanced Manufacturing as they honored Senator Durbin for his lifetime of service to the Quad Cities.

The Quad Cities is a better, stronger community because of his leadership in the U.S. Senate, and I hope I can make him proud and continue the work.

.@IllinoisStateU's new College of Engineering in Bloomington is AMAZING! Thanks to Dr. Tarhule and the team for the tour.

How great is it that the next generation of technological leaders will be Redbirds? https://t.co/SMiBxJJpvB

Derek from Team Sorensen helped celebrate the ribbon cutting for @Fareway_Stores in Coal Valley!

Families in this part of Rock Island County will finally have what they deserve: a full-service grocery store with a real meat counter, fresh produce, and the basics you need for https://t.co/RgdYHasc0L

Had a blast in East Moline celebrating the revitalization of the historic downtown, which will create new opportunities for residents, local businesses, and visitors alike!

These improvements would not have been possible without Senator Durbin and my predecessor and friend, https://t.co/g6OUNL0WaK

Thank you to Rolando and the team at Rancho Supermarket for allowing me to see the wonderful work being done to serve our neighbors in Rockford!

Watch and take the tour with me! https://t.co/f8o2LvyRK7

Today’s Election Day! Get out and make your voices heard!

Visit https://t.co/12xeCBScCw to check your registration and polling location. https://t.co/DD1sx51v8K

Thank you to the Bloomington/Normal Police Chiefs and Sheriffs Group—especially TJ Jennings, President of the IL Drug Enforcement Officers, for letting me sit-in on your monthly meeting!

Law enforcement put their lives on the line to protect our neighbors every day, and I will always support and work with them to address the challenges they face.
https://t.co/KvUycWN675

Rock Island's West End was filled with joy as we cut the ribbon on the new Skip-a-Long Childhood Center!

Head Start providers are essential for increasing education access, combating food insecurity, and giving children the chance to make their dreams come true.

Thank you to everyone who made this celebration a massive success!

Many thanks to the dozens of seniors at Westminster Village for speaking with me about how we fight to safeguard Social Security for them and for their children and grandchildren. 

Thanks for having me! https://t.co/mxmd6eceWK

Always a good day when I can have lunch with my friend Bartonville Mayor Leon Ricca—especially at an amazing local spot like Jim's!

Thanks for taking the time Mayor, and I look forward to our continued work together. https://t.co/JE2AcxD4FV

Sprague’s Super Service on Route 66 in Normal is aces!

Had a great time talking with Terri, who restored this building to its 1930s glory, and learning about the history of the national road. https://t.co/08sQri0M69

Community Health Care Clinic and their "Mighty Nine" are helping make doctors, dentists, and mental health services more accessible in McLean County.
 
Great to meet with their team, learn more about their mission, and discuss how we can work together to make healthcare accessible for everyone.

GOP cuts to SNAP and the high cost of food (because of fuel costs) are making things dire for thousands of people in our district.

I am especially thankful to faith leaders in Peoria for sitting down with me to talk about the need. I will never stop fighting to lower the costs for the people who need it the most.
https://t.co/nUWcLmWrl4

Congratulations to @WesternILUniv for being named one of the Midwest's best colleges for the 22nd time!

We are leading the way right here at home. Stoked for the national recognition! 🔗⬇️ https://t.co/u45dgsAXS4

Super cool news out of the @USDA_ARS's AgLab in Peoria!

Using crickets to help farmers get the most out of their corn crops—a trend we can all hop on!

Read more: https://t.co/FusXERTPxP

My office, like many Congressional offices across the country, received a suspicious envelope this morning.

My team has trained for all kinds of situations and I am happy to report everyone is safe. I am grateful to the Rockford Police and Fire Departments, as well as the FBI

High School students: there's still time to submit your application for Congressional Nomination to one of our prestigious U.S. Service Academies.

It is an honor to be but a small part of this process, helping give #IL17's young people a chance to make their dreams come true.

Learn more below!

So excited for @rvcgoldeneagles and the new opportunities for people in Downtown Rockford.

From automotive tech to law enforcement training, this is another example of doing it right in Rockford!

I was especially impressed speaking with a 17 year old student who turns 18 in just a few weeks and is excited to vote for the first time!

A “Diverging Diamond” is coming to IL-17! Soon, there will be no crossing traffic at the interchange of I-74 and John Deere Road. Instead, a more seamless flow of traffic that will keep us moving forward.

Team Sorensen was on hand for the official groundbreaking ceremony that will put hundreds of people to work and improve the commute for thousands of Quad Citizens.

Thank you to @IDOT_Illinois for investing in #IL17!

Team Sorensen was happy to attend a ribbon cutting ceremony for the Illinois Army National Guard’s new Field Maintenance Shop in Bloomington!

Grateful to all our partners who helped make this project happen. And as a member of @HASCDemocrats, I’ll continue fighting for the support all our National Guardsmen deserve.

There's still time to submit your entries for the Congressional App Challenge!

Can't wait to see all the amazing things our IL-17 middle- and high-school students can create!

Learn more: https://t.co/VrBTy1bLqZ

Today is #NationalComingOutDay, a time to celebrate and embrace our LGBTQ+ friends, neighbors and loved ones.

Whether this is your 30th year celebrating, or maybe you're still not ready: know you are seen, heard and loved.

Being one of only 13 present Members of Congress who have personally celebrated this day is an honor. 🏳️‍🌈

MCL Health is bringing high-quality healthcare to Operators, Carpenters, and Teamsters all across IL-17, and it was a pleasure to tour their new Rock Island facility and thank them for their dedicated work.

Awesome to get a sneak peek of the renovated Operators 150 Hall, too...can’t wait for it to open soon!

Mike Ditka was Chicago football. Tough, loud and fiercely loyal to this city and this team.

He gave this young Bears fan the ‘85 championship and set a standard we’ve been chasing ever since.

Rest in peace, Coach. Thinking of his family and all of Bears Nation. 🐻⬇️ https://t.co/ioqFoeKSg9

As a Meteorologist, I know that disasters don’t discriminate blue states versus red states.

The purpose of a disaster declaration is to help families pick up the pieces and start on the path toward rebuilding their lives, and the mere idea that the Trump administration would play games with this is ridiculous.

I will keep fighting for the full recovery our families deserve.
https://t.co/iZXFBms0uZ

🚨Attention IL-17 Students and Parents🚨

Each year, I have the honor and privilege of nominating young people from our district to our prestigious U.S. Service Academies. Are you or someone you know interested in applying?

Learn more below! Applications close November 1st. https://t.co/gaE0cKHKAC

Today marks three years since the deadly terrorist attacks in Israel.

In honor of those who lost their lives, we must recommit ourselves to the cause of peace for all people and ensure everyone has the basic health and security they need and deserve.

This Hispanic Heritage Month, I’m proud to recognize and celebrate the incredible history, rich culture, and ongoing contributions of the Hispanic community in America.

At a time when so many seek to divide us and turn neighbor against neighbor—I hope we can take this time to embrace one another with open arms and move forward towards a brighter future for all.

High costs aren't only hurting our families, they're also squeezing local small businesses like Supermercado Monarca in East Moline.

Proud to stand beside Saul and his incredible team to discuss my work to lower costs and provide the relief our neighbors need and deserve. https://t.co/mCmbrUGCts

Thank you to the brave men and women of the Illinois Army National Guard’s Readiness Center in Peoria for showing me around your facility.

As a member of @hascdemocrats, one of my top priorities is supporting National Guardsmen around the country—to ensure they always have the tools and resources they need to complete their critical missions.

Thank you for all you do!

Big win for the workers at FCI Thomson! You deserve the safety and certainty provided by a union contract.

Grateful to @AfgeLocal4070 for your advocacy on behalf of our workers. Proud to be with you in the fight for everyone's collective bargaining rights. https://t.co/aS17S5Agos

IL-17's bringing home some hardware!

Team Sorensen was proud to attend a ceremony celebrating the 2026 Airport of the Year Award Winners, three of which are right here in our District!

Congratulations to the winners, and thank you for your continued dedication to our community. https://t.co/9Zz6llOxmT

Illinois Central College is one of Peoria’s crown jewels, setting our young people on paths to fulfilling, successful careers right here in Central Illinois.

It was a joy to tour their health sciences department and get an update on their incredible work (and get a quick check-up while I was at it!)

Thanks for having me!

Glad to help break ground on Peoria Heights’ new water filtration plant.

Clean water is one of those things nobody thinks about until it’s gone, and I’m happy I could help bring federal funding home so this community has safe drinking water for the next 100 years. https://t.co/nCW7r7S5rJ

Exciting news in Peoria!

The @AmeriCorps National Civilian Community Corps is partnering with the @PeoriaParkDist to help restore native habitats, improve park trails, and support local events.

Can't wait to see the results!

Awesome to be the first person to use the new EV fast-chargers at the East Moline Public Library.

Proud to drive my UAW, American-made Chevy Bolt and it’s so important to bring charging access to everyone, regardless if they have the ability to charge at home.

Thank you @Metrolink, the State of Illinois, and the City of EM in getting this done!

Just one month left to submit your entries for the Congressional App Challenge!

Can't wait to see all the amazing entries from middle- and high-school students from IL-17!

Learn more: https://t.co/VrBTy1bLqZ https://t.co/JTqK9GarXm

Attention all weather geeks! I am happy to kick off @eesionline's briefing on Super El Niño today!

It's important we learn as much as we can about this seasonal forecast and the possibilities for severe weather.

Follow along: https://t.co/0TlRaousbd

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
